escalation.rationale: Score remains High as Ukraine launches a mass drone attack on Moscow (1,600 intercepted since Saturday), the US-Iran war cost reaches $43.6B, Houthis tighten Red Sea grip prompting Saudi escalation warnings, and Iran's IRGC strikes an oil tanker in the Strait of Hormuz — slightly reduced from yesterday due to marginal crude price relief and diplomatic signals including China pressuring Iran to rein in Houthis.

ticker_items: Ukraine fires mass drone attack on Moscow; Russia claims 1,600 intercepted since Saturday.
US-Iran war cost hits $43.6B; weapons bill alone reaches $28.1B.
Houthis seize Red Sea choke point; Saudi Arabia warns of 'very sizeable response.'
Iran's IRGC reportedly strikes oil tanker in Strait of Hormuz.
US-Denmark strike deal on Greenland military presence; Pentagon weighs Europe troop cuts.

eastern_europe.description: Ukraine launched a mass drone attack on Moscow; Russian authorities claim 1,600 drones intercepted since Saturday including approximately 450 directed at the capital, with two killed.

middle_east.description: Iran's Revolutionary Guards reportedly struck an oil tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, according to Iranian media cited by Haaretz.
Israeli forces shelled positions in southern Lebanon injuring two people before withdrawing from the outskirts of a town after a standoff with Lebanese forces.
Houthi forces exchanged cross-border drone, missile, and aircraft strikes with Saudi Arabia as the Houthi-Saudi conflict continued with Yemeni civilian displacement reported.

observers.description: China privately pressured Iran to rein in Houthi proxies and reopen the Strait of Hormuz after Iran failed to secure international support at BRICS. China continues to publicly advocate for world peace while navigating economic ties with both US and Iran.

Saudi Arabia is actively exchanging cross-border strikes with Houthi forces in Yemen following Houthi seizure of a key Red Sea choke point affecting Saudi oil shipments. Analysts warn a major Saudi military response is imminent. Saudi Arabia is simultaneously seeking to restore East-West pipeline operations to ease supply disruptions.

South Korean President Lee Jae Myung confirmed Seoul will not deploy troops to the Strait of Hormuz or join the US war on Iran. South Korea indicated willingness to facilitate US-North Korea dialogue as Trump signals interest in Pyongyang talks.

Bavarian Premier Markus Söder called for Ukraine aid to generate German arms orders and secure access to Ukrainian raw materials, reflecting Berlin's increasingly transactional approach to Kyiv support. Germany also established a drone defense research center following the Leipzig incident.

The US is actively engaged in the Iran war at a cost of $43.6B with the weapons bill at $28.1B. The Pentagon is simultaneously weighing a reduction of one-third of troops from Europe. A deal was reached with Denmark on expanding US military presence in Greenland. Domestic political pressure on Defense Secretary Hegseth intensified with impeachment articles introduced related to the Iran war.

British military sites were targeted by drones hundreds of times in the past year amid heightened tensions with Russia and Iran. UK officials are under pressure to take the Russian threat to NATO states more seriously following warnings from Polish and French leaders.
Denmark reached a deal with the United States to bolster US military presence in Greenland, ending months of diplomatic tension during which Trump threatened to take the island by force.

financial.notes: Crude oil fell for a third consecutive session as Saudi Arabia moved to restore East-West pipeline operations, easing supply fears despite lingering Strait of Hormuz risk from Iran's IRGC tanker strike and Houthi Red Sea activity.

update_log.text: Ukraine mass drone attack on Moscow kills two; Russia claims 1,600 drones intercepted since Saturday including ~450 targeting the capital.
Saudi analyst warns of 'very sizeable' Saudi military response to escalating Houthi attacks on Red Sea shipping routes.
Iran's IRGC reported to have struck an oil tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, according to Iranian media cited by Haaretz.
US-Denmark announce deal to expand American military presence in Greenland following months of Trump pressure on Copenhagen.
Pentagon reportedly considering proposals to reduce US troop presence in Europe by up to one-third, per Al Jazeera.
US Central Command reports Iran war total cost at $43.6B as of September 3, with weapons expenditure hitting $28.1B.
Israel shells southern Lebanon injuring two; Israeli forces withdraw from town outskirts after standoff with Lebanese army.
China privately urged Iran to rein in Houthis and reopen Strait of Hormuz after Iran failed to secure BRICS support.
War on the Rocks analysis: Iran war is degrading US military readiness through munitions consumption, interceptor depletion, and extended deployments.
Houthis consolidate control over key Red Sea choke point affecting Saudi oil shipments; Saudi-Houthi cross-border strikes continue.
